$comment: The environment manifest for the CLOUDFLARE preview track. Paste it into a `remote-custom`
infra handler (Infrastructure -> Test environments) on the workspace that develops
cat-factory, register the secret `githubToken`, and point the backend service frame at it
with provisioning { type: 'custom', manifestId: 'cat-factory-cloudflare-preview' }.
See ../README.md and ../../../docs/dogfooding.md for the full walkthrough.
The management API is GITHUB'S OWN Deployments API: no bespoke control-plane service to run,
and every call is plain outbound HTTPS — which is what makes it work from the Cloudflare
Worker facade, where there is no Docker daemon and no filesystem.
provision -> POST a deployment for the PR head. GitHub fires the `deployment` event, which
runs .github/workflows/preview-env.yml, and echoes our `payload` back in the
response — which is where the environment URL comes from.
teardown  -> POST an `inactive` status on that deployment, which fires the workflow's
teardown job (deletes the per-PR Worker and its D1 databases).
TWO DELIBERATE CHOICES, both consequences of the generic HTTP backend settling a provision
SYNCHRONOUSLY (what the provision call returns is what the deployer records and the tester
is handed — there is no poll-until-ready for this backend):
1. `url` comes from the request's own payload, not from the deploy. The per-PR Worker name
is ours to choose, so `https://cat-factory-pr-<n>.<subdomain>.workers.dev` is knowable
before anything is built. Substitute your account's workers.dev subdomain below.
Reading it back from the deploy instead would hand the tester `null`.
2. There is NO `status` request. Without one the backend echoes what provision captured
(ready + that URL) on every refresh. With one, the GitHub statuses endpoint returns an
ARRAY whose shape does not carry the payload, so a refresh would map the URL back to
null and erase it. The workflow still writes real statuses — they are the human-facing
record on the PR, and the `inactive` one is the teardown trigger.
The readiness window this leaves (a deployment registered before its build finishes) is what
the workflow's `pull_request` trigger closes: the environment is built when the branch is
pushed, minutes before a pipeline reaches its deployer step.
Replace OWNER/REPO and SUBDOMAIN, then register the secret `githubToken`: a fine-grained
token on that repo with Deployments: read & write and nothing else. Provision inputs
available here are {{input.branch}}, {{input.pullNumber}}, {{input.repoOwner}},
{{input.repoName}}, {{input.blockId}} and {{input.pullUrl}}.
label: cat-factory preview (Cloudflare, via GitHub Deployments)
